9185.t: Of unknown origin. Perhaps related to ἀσκός (askós, “skin, hide”), thus with original meaning "to prepare a skin".

9168.t: From ἀρόω (ăróō, “I plow”) + -τήρ (-tḗr, masculine agent noun suffix). See also ἄροτρον (árotron).

9179.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂ér-ye-, a ye-present from the root *h₂erh₃- (“to plough”). Cognates include Old Armenian արաւր (arawr), Latin arō, Old Church Slavonic орати (orati), and Old English erian (Early Modern English ear).

9173.t: From ἀρχή (arkhḗ, “beginning”) + ἡγέομαι (hēgéomai, “to lead”) + -της (-tēs, masculine agentive suffix).

9189.t: From ἀστήρ (astḗr, “star”) + λέγω (légō, “to compute, to reckon”) + -ος (-os).

9187.t: Solmsen connected σπαλύσσεται (spalússetai, “to rip, agitate”) and σφαλάσσειν (sphalássein, “to cut, sting”), but this is semantically unconvincing. It is rather a Pre-Greek word in view of the suffix, typical of plant names.

9170.t: This verb is generally reconstructed as *ἀϝερτάω (*ăwertắō), from ἀείρω (ăeírō, “to bind; to hang”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wer- (“to raise; to bind”); however, the derivation is unusual.

9152.t: According to Beekes, from a Proto-Indo-European *h₂reh₁ǵ- (“to help, support”). Cognates include Proto-Germanic *rōkijaną (“to take care of”).

9178.t: From ἀρχή (arkhḗ, “a beginning, origin”) + -θεν (-then, “a suffix added to nouns to form adverbs of place from which: from”)

9197.t: From ἄσχολος (ắskholos, “occupied, busy”) + -ία (-íā, abstract noun suffix).

9133.t: From ἀπο- (apo-, “away from”) + φεύγω (pheúgō, “to flee, run off”).
